newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees similar rules for late fall CRP sign-up.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees similar rules for late fall CRP sign-up.

text.p: The next "sign-up" for the Conservation Reserve Program will come in late fall, possibly October or November, U.S. Agriculture Department officials said Wednesday.
Parks Shackleford, a Farm Service Agency official, said maximum county rental rates would be the same as a "sign-up" held in March and eligibility rules would be similar.
Sign-up probably would not begin until FSA completes paperwork on the 16.1 million acres accepted from the March bidding and pays annual farm subsidies due in September.
Land expiring in 1998 would be eligible for the sign-up.

Shackleford said USDA would consider, for land accepted from the fall sign-up, making payments begin upon date of acceptance. But, he said, it could not make the payments retroactive to this October, an idea suggested by Representative Larry Combest, Texas Republican.

Under questioning from Combest at a House Agriculture subcommittee hearing, Shackleford said the next signup would be held during the fall. The season begins September 20 and ends December 22, Combest said.

Shackleford and other USDA officials at the hearing cautioned that the cut-off point for accepting land into CRP could be different than in March. Land is assigned a score under an Environmental Benefit Index. The scores provide a comparison among bids but ranking among bids can be affected by volume of land offered and benefits to be gained from each.
